title: Sign Language Visual Semiotic Decoder Using Deep Learning Approach
content: Human communication is essential for social and cognitive development, but not everyone has equal access due to sensory disabilities, such as hearing impairments. These affect 25% of people with sensory disabilities, and it is projected that by 2050, the number of people with hearing loss will reach 2.5 billion. Sign language becomes a crucial tool for the social integration of deaf individuals, although its regional variability and limited inclusion in essential services pose challenges. This study proposes a new sign language translation methodology using a deep learning architecture that models gestures through semiotic analysis, overcoming limitations observed in other approaches. The system, tested with 10, 30, 100, 150, 220, 320, 480, 700, and 1171 synthetic gestures of representative sign language vocabulary, showed an accuracy of 99.65% in Cohen’s Kappa coefficient and Matthews Correlation Coefficient, highlighting its potential to improve real-time communication between deaf and hearing people.
